mutants.name: Cyrillic homoglyph smuggled into Latin text is caught (ѕоundalike)
planted file on disk is caught by the file-scan path (and cleaned up)
allowlist is load-bearing: without it, the LÖVR line would fail the gate
Latin text (symbols included) passes the gate — no false positives

limitations: Script detection covers 14 non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Han, Kana, Hangul, Arabic, Hebrew, Greek, Thai, Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, Georgian, Armenian); an exotic script outside this set would not be caught.
Typographic symbols (— ✓ ✗ … ⚠ →) are script-neutral and allowed by design; M33.S4 remains the per-string English gate on help surfaces.
Gate C scans the enumerated CLI surfaces; a new command's help is covered only once added to the surface list (M33.S4 parity gate flags undeclared commands, which closes that gap).
